name: Sulayman ibn Harb
nameAr: سليمان بن حرب بن بجيل الأزدي الواشحي البصري

nisbas.en: al-Washihi (a clan of al-Azd; Ibn Hajar spells it: dotted shin, then undotted ha)

bornNote: Safar 140 AH, by his own statement as al-Bukhari reports it (al-Dhahabi, Siyar).
diedNote: Rabi' al-Akhir 224 AH, in Basra, aged eighty (Ibn Sa'd and others; the Taqrib).

deathVariants.authority: Ibn Sa'd and others; Ibn Hajar, Taqrib
deathVariants.source: Siyar A'lam al-Nubala' (Wikisource); Taqrib al-Tahdhib, entry 2545

deathVariants.authority: variants listed in the Shamela narrator record

taqrib.ar: ثقة إمام حافظ من التاسعة، مات سنة أربع وعشرين وله ثمانون سنة
taqrib.en: Reliable, an imam, a hadith master; of the ninth generation; died in 224 aged eighty.

role: Teacher of al-Bukhari; judge of Makkah

teachers.name: Hammad ibn Zayd
teachers.source: Sahih al-Bukhari 3688; Tahdhib al-Tahdhib, entry on Hammad ibn Zayd (students); al-Dhahabi, Siyar: 'when Shu'bah died I sat with Hammad ibn Zayd for nineteen years until he died'

students.name: al-Humaydi
students.source: al-Dhahabi, Siyar: 'and al-Humaydi, who died before him'

students.name: Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan
students.source: al-Dhahabi, Siyar: 'and, among the earlier men, Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan and Ahmad ibn Hanbal'

students.name: Ahmad ibn Hanbal
students.source: al-Dhahabi, Siyar; Tahdhib al-Tahdhib 2/88 (via Shamela): 'we wrote from Sulayman ibn Harb while Ibn Uyaynah was alive'

verdicts.ar: سليمان بن حرب إمام من الأئمة، كان لا يدلس، ويتكلم في الرجال وفي الفقه
verdicts.en: Sulayman ibn Harb is an imam among the imams; he did not use the ambiguous formula, and he spoke on narrators and on law.

verdicts.ar: كان سليمان بن حرب قلّ من يرضى من المشايخ، فإذا رأيته قد روى عن شيخ فاعلم أنه ثقة
verdicts.en: Sulayman ibn Harb was satisfied with few teachers; when you see him narrating from a man, know that the man is reliable.

verdicts.ar: حدثنا سليمان بن حرب، وكان ثقة ثبتا صاحب حفظ
verdicts.en: Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us; he was reliable, firm, a man of memory.

verdicts.ar: كان ثقة كثير الحديث، وقد ولي قضاء مكة ثم عزل فرجع إلى البصرة
verdicts.en: He was reliable and prolific; he held the judgeship of Makkah, was removed, and returned to Basra.

verdicts.via: describing the Basran shaykhs to the caliph al-Ma'mun
verdicts.ar: هو ثقة حافظ للحديث عاقل في نهاية الستر والصيانة
verdicts.en: He is reliable, a memoriser of hadith, sensible, of the utmost probity and self-restraint.

verdicts.ar: كان سليمان بن حرب يحدث بالحديث ثم يحدث به كأنه ليس ذاك
verdicts.en: Sulayman ibn Harb would narrate a hadith, then narrate it again as if it were not the same (a note on his narrating by sense).

verdicts.ar: كان يروي على المعنى فيغير ألفاظه
verdicts.en: He narrated according to the sense, so his wording would change.

flags.label: Narrated by sense
flags.detail: Abu Dawud and al-Khatib record that he transmitted the meaning rather than the fixed wording, so the same report could come out in different words. The critics who note it still rank him among the firmest; it is a reason to compare his wording with other students of Hammad ibn Zayd, not a reason to doubt the report.

bio: A Basran of al-Azd, born in 140, who began seeking hadith in 158, attended Shu'bah until Shu'bah died and then sat with Hammad ibn Zayd for nineteen years. Al-Ma'mun appointed him judge of Makkah; al-Khatib dates the appointment to 214 and his removal to 219, after which he returned to Basra. He narrated from memory and was known for accepting few teachers, so that Abu Hatim took his narrating from a man as itself a sign of that man's reliability. Al-Bukhari, Abu Dawud, al-Humaydi and Ahmad ibn Hanbal are among his students. He died in Basra in Rabi' al-Akhir 224.
